units.title: Present simple and present continuous
units.summary: Facts, habits and routines versus actions happening now or around now.

cards.title: Present simple: facts and habits
cards.body: Use the present simple for things that are **always or generally true**, for **habits and routines**, and for **timetables**.
examples: Water boils at 100°C.
I usually study in the evening.
The exam starts at 9 a.m.

cards.title: Present continuous: now and around now
cards.body: Use the present continuous for actions **happening at the moment of speaking**, **temporary situations**, and **changing trends**.
examples: I'm reading a novel at the moment.
She's living with her aunt this term.
More people are working from home.

cards.title: Form
rows: He doesn't work · They don't work
Does she work? · Do they work?
I am / she is / they are working

items: She work in a hospital.
She works in a hospital.
Add -s for he/she/it.
I am usually going to the gym on Mondays.
I usually go to the gym on Mondays.
Routines use the present simple.
Prices rise at the moment.
Prices are rising at the moment.
An ongoing change uses the continuous.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: In **Speaking Part 1**, routines need the present simple. In **Task 1**, use the present simple to describe what a chart *shows*, and the present continuous for trends that are still happening.
examples: I usually cycle to university because it's quicker than the bus.
The graph shows the number of tourists visiting three countries.
The use of electric cars is growing rapidly.

practice.q: Look! It ___ outside.
My brother ___ in a bank. He has worked there for years.
The table ___ (show) the average income in four countries.
practice.x: Describing what a chart shows → present simple.

practice.q: Right now, I ___ (prepare) for my IELTS exam.
practice.x: An action in progress around now.

practice.q: She [go] to the library every Saturday.
practice.x: He/she/it takes -s in the present simple.

practice.q: These days, more students [choose] to study online.
practice.x: A current, changing trend → present continuous.

practice.q: Which sentence is correct?
practice.x: 'Know' is a state verb; it is not used in the continuous.

practice.q: The train ___ at 6.45 tomorrow morning.
practice.x: Timetables use the present simple, even for the future.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: The number of online learners is increasing every year.

units.title: State verbs
units.summary: Verbs that describe states, not actions, and are not normally used in continuous forms.

cards.title: States, not actions
cards.body:
Some verbs describe a **state**: thoughts, feelings, possession and senses. They are not normally used in the continuous form.
- **Thinking:** know, believe, understand, mean, remember
- **Feelings:** like, love, hate, prefer, want, need
- **Possession:** have (= own), own, belong, include
- **Being:** seem, appear, consist, contain, depend
examples: I believe that education should be free.
This book belongs to my teacher.
The course includes four modules.

cards.title: Verbs with two meanings
cards.body: Some verbs are states in one meaning and actions in another.
examples: I think it's a good idea. (opinion → state)
I'm thinking about my answer. (process → action)
She has two cars. (possession)
She's having lunch. (action)

items: I am believing that governments should act.
I believe that governments should act.
'Believe' is a state verb.
The price is depending on the season.
The price depends on the season.
'Depend' is a state verb.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Opinion verbs appear in every Task 2 essay and Part 3 answer. Using them in the continuous is a noticeable grammar error.
examples: I strongly believe that public transport should be free.
Many people feel that cities are becoming too crowded.

practice.q: I ___ what you mean.
We ___ dinner at the moment; can I call you back?
practice.x: 'Have dinner' is an action, so the continuous is fine.

practice.q: Many people are [preferring] to shop online.
This essay ___ (contain) three main arguments.
Which sentence is correct?
o: The success of a policy is depending on funding.
The success of a policy depends on funding.
The success of a policy depend on funding.
practice.a: The success of a policy depends on funding.

practice.q: I ___ of moving abroad next year.
practice.x: 'Think about/of' as a mental process → continuous is possible.

practice.q: Nowadays everyone is [owning] a smartphone.
It ___ (seem) that technology has changed education completely.

units.title: Past simple and past continuous
units.summary: Finished past actions, and background actions in progress at a past moment.

cards.title: Past simple: finished actions
cards.body: Use the past simple for **completed actions at a definite past time**. It is the main tense for Task 1 charts with past dates.
examples: Sales rose sharply in 2010.
I visited Sylhet last summer.
The number of visitors fell to 2 million in 2015.

cards.title: Past continuous: the background
cards.body: Use the past continuous for an **action in progress at a past moment**, often interrupted by a shorter action in the past simple.
examples: I was studying when the power went off.
At 8 p.m. we were waiting for the results.
While she was living in Dhaka, she learned to cook.

cards.title: Form
rows: work → worked · study → studied · stop → stopped
rise → rose · fall → fell · grow → grew · see → saw

items: The price raised in 2005.
The price rose in 2005.
'Rise' is intransitive: rise – rose – risen.
I didn't went to class.
I didn't go to class.
After 'did/didn't' use the base form.
When I arrived, they had dinner.
When I arrived, they were having dinner.
Use the continuous for the action already in progress.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: In **Task 1**, if the dates are in the past, the whole report is in the past. In **Part 2**, stories need past simple for events and past continuous for background.
examples: Car ownership grew steadily between 1990 and 2010, while bus use declined.
I was walking home from school when I first saw the old house.

practice.q: The number of students ___ (fall) to 300 in 2018.
Exports ___ (rise) significantly between 2000 and 2010.
I ___ for the bus when it started to rain.
Unemployment [raised] to 8% in 2009.
She didn't [finished] her essay on time.
Which sentence describes past data correctly?
o: In 1990, coal provides 50% of the electricity.
In 1990, coal provided 50% of the electricity.
In 1990, coal was providing 50% of the electricity.
practice.a: In 1990, coal provided 50% of the electricity.
practice.x: A finished past time → past simple.

practice.q: While I ___ (study) abroad, I made many friends.
The figure ___ at 45% in 2000 and then dropped.
practice.x: A single completed event in Task 1.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: Bus use declined steadily over the period.

units.title: Present perfect
units.summary: Past actions connected to now: experience, change, unfinished time.

cards.title: Connecting past and present
cards.body:
Use the present perfect when the past action **matters now** and **no finished time** is given:
- **Experience:** I have visited India twice.
- **Change up to now:** Technology has changed the way we learn.
- **Unfinished time:** I have read three books this month.
- **With for/since:** She has lived here since 2015.
examples: The internet has transformed communication.
Air pollution has become a serious problem in many cities.

cards.title: Form
rows: + a starting point: since 2010, since I was a child

items: I have seen him yesterday.
I saw him yesterday.
A finished time (yesterday) needs the past simple.
She lives here since 2015.
She has lived here since 2015.
'Since' + up to now → present perfect.
Technology has change our lives.
Technology has changed our lives.
Use the past participle.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Task 2 introductions often describe recent change. The present perfect is the natural tense for this.
examples: In recent years, online shopping has become increasingly popular.
Governments have tried many ways to reduce traffic, with mixed results.

practice.q: In recent decades, the cost of living ___ (increase) dramatically.
practice.x: Change up to now → present perfect.

practice.q: I ___ to Cox's Bazar three times.
I ___ to Cox's Bazar last year.
practice.x: 'Last year' is a finished time → past simple.

practice.q: She has worked here ___ 2019.
They have been friends ___ ten years.
I have [finish] my homework already.
Smartphones [changed] the way people communicate in recent years.
Which sentence is correct?
o: I have met her two days ago.
I met her two days ago.
I have meet her two days ago.
practice.a: I met her two days ago.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: Online learning has become increasingly popular in recent years.

units.title: Present perfect continuous
units.summary: Activities that started in the past and are still continuing, or have just stopped with visible results.

cards.title: Duration up to now
cards.body: Use **have/has been + -ing** to emphasise **how long** an activity has continued up to now.
examples: I have been learning English for six years.
It has been raining since this morning.
Researchers have been studying this problem for decades.

cards.title: Simple or continuous?
cards.body: The **present perfect simple** focuses on the **result or number**. The **continuous** focuses on the **activity and its duration**.
examples: I have written three essays this week. (result)
I have been writing essays all week. (activity)

items: I am studying English for five years.
I have been studying English for five years.
Duration up to now needs the present perfect.
I have been knowing him for years.
I have known him for years.
State verbs don't take the continuous.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: A very common Speaking Part 1 question is 'How long have you…?'. Answer with the present perfect continuous.
examples: I've been living in Chattogram for about ten years now.
I've been working as a junior engineer since I graduated.

practice.q: I ___ (wait) for an hour. Where were you?
She ___ three chapters so far.
practice.x: A number of completed things → simple.

practice.q: Why are your eyes red? — I ___ for hours.
practice.x: A recent activity with a visible result.

practice.q: I [am living] in this city since 2012.
We have been [knowing] each other since school.
practice.x: 'Know' is a state verb → have known.

practice.q: Scientists ___ (research) climate change for over fifty years.
Which answer fits 'How long have you studied English?'
o: I study English for eight years.
I've been studying English for about eight years.
I was studying English for eight years.
practice.a: I've been studying English for about eight years.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: I have been preparing for this exam since January.

units.title: Past perfect
units.summary: The 'past before the past': which of two past events happened first.

cards.title: Earlier past
cards.body: Use **had + past participle** for an action that happened **before another past action or time**.
examples: When I arrived, the lecture had already started.
By 2010, the population had doubled.
She told me she had lost her passport.

cards.title: Past perfect continuous
cards.body: Use **had been + -ing** for an activity that continued up to a past moment.
examples: I had been studying for three hours when my friend called.

items: When we got there, the film already started.
When we got there, the film had already started.
The film started first.
By 2005 sales have reached a peak.
By 2005 sales had reached a peak.
'By' + past time → past perfect.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: In **Task 1**, 'by + past year' is a natural place for the past perfect. In **Part 2**, it shows the order of events in your story.
examples: By 1990, the number of cars had risen to 20 million.
I had never seen the sea before I visited Cox's Bazar.

practice.q: By the time the ambulance arrived, the man ___ (leave).
practice.x: He left before the ambulance arrived.

practice.q: By 2000, the figure ___ to 50%.
I realised I [forgot] my keys at home.
She ___ for two hours when the bus finally came.
practice.x: Duration up to a past moment.

practice.q: Which sentence shows the correct order of events?
o: After he had finished the exam, he went home.
After he has finished the exam, he went home.
After he finishing the exam, he went home.
practice.a: After he had finished the exam, he went home.

practice.q: I ___ (never/fly) before my trip to Malaysia.
Put the words in order.
practice.a: By 2015, the number of users had tripled.

units.title: used to, would, be used to
units.summary: Past habits that have stopped, and being or getting accustomed to something.

cards.title: used to + base verb
cards.body: Past habits or states that are **no longer true**.
examples: I used to live in a village.
People used to write letters instead of emails.
Did you use to play cricket?

cards.title: would for past habits
cards.body: **Would** can describe repeated past actions (not states), often in stories.
examples: Every summer we would visit our grandparents.

cards.title: be / get used to + -ing
cards.body: **Be used to** = be accustomed to. **Get used to** = become accustomed to. Both are followed by a noun or **-ing**.
examples: I'm used to waking up early.
It took me months to get used to the cold weather.

items: I am used to wake up early.
I am used to waking up early.
'To' is a preposition here → -ing.
I use to play football.
I used to play football.
The past form is 'used to'.
I would live in Khulna as a child.
I used to live in Khulna as a child.
'Would' is not used for past states.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Part 1 and Part 3 often compare **past and present**. 'Used to' makes these comparisons natural.
examples: When I was a child, I used to read comics, but now I mostly read on my phone.
People used to rely on newspapers for news, whereas now social media is the main source.

practice.q: I ___ like vegetables, but now I love them.
practice.x: A past state that has changed.

practice.q: She has lived in London for years, so she ___ the rain.
I'm not used to ___ (drive) on the left.
People [use] to travel by boat before the bridge was built.
It took me a while to get used to [live] alone.
Which sentence is correct?
o: My grandfather would be a farmer.
My grandfather used to be a farmer.
My grandfather was used to be a farmer.
practice.a: My grandfather used to be a farmer.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: People used to spend more time outdoors.

units.title: Future forms
units.summary: will, be going to and the present continuous for predictions, plans and arrangements.

cards.title: will
cards.body: Use **will** for predictions based on opinion, sudden decisions, promises and offers.
examples: I think robots will replace many jobs.
I'll help you with that.

cards.title: be going to
cards.body: Use **be going to** for plans already decided and predictions based on present evidence.
examples: I'm going to take the IELTS exam in March.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.

cards.title: Present continuous for arrangements
cards.body: Use the present continuous for fixed arrangements with a time.
examples: I'm meeting my tutor on Friday.

items: I will to study abroad.
I will study abroad.
No 'to' after will.
When I will finish university, I will travel.
When I finish university, I will travel.
After when/if/as soon as, use the present for the future.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Part 3 asks about the future. Mix **will**, **be likely to** and **may** to show range and avoid over-certainty.
examples: In the future, I think most people will work from home at least part of the week.
Cities are likely to become even more crowded unless public transport improves.

practice.q: I've bought the tickets. We ___ visit Sajek next week.
I'm sure technology ___ change education even more.
As soon as I ___ (get) my results, I'll call you.
practice.x: Present tense after 'as soon as' for the future.

practice.q: If the government [will invest] in transport, traffic will improve.
Which sentence is correct?
o: I am going to visit my aunt tomorrow.
I going to visit my aunt tomorrow.
I will to visit my aunt tomorrow.
practice.a: I am going to visit my aunt tomorrow.

practice.q: The phone is ringing. — I ___ answer it.
practice.x: A decision at the moment of speaking.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: More people are likely to work from home in the future.

units.title: Future continuous and future perfect
units.summary: Actions in progress at a future time, and actions completed before a future time.

cards.title: Future continuous
cards.body: **will be + -ing** for an action in progress at a future time.
examples: This time next year, I will be studying in Canada.

cards.title: Future perfect
cards.body: **will have + past participle** for an action completed **by** a future time. Very useful for Task 1 projections.
examples: By 2050, the world's population will have reached nearly 10 billion.
By the end of the course, you will have written twenty essays.

items: By 2030, the figure will double.
By 2030, the figure will have doubled.
'By' + future time → future perfect.
Tomorrow at 9 I will sit the exam.
Tomorrow at 9 I will be sitting the exam.
In progress at that time → future continuous.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Charts often show **projections** (e.g. 2030, 2050). Use future forms with 'is projected / expected to'.
examples: The proportion of older people is projected to rise to 25% by 2050.
By 2040, renewable energy will have overtaken coal.

practice.q: By 2035, sales of electric cars ___ (overtake) petrol cars.
At 8 p.m. tonight I ___ for my flight.
practice.x: In progress at a future moment.

practice.q: By next year, I will [finish] my degree.
The number of users is expected ___ 2 billion by 2030.
Which sentence describes a projection correctly?
o: By 2050, the figure will has risen to 40%.
By 2050, the figure will have risen to 40%.
By 2050, the figure has risen to 40%.
practice.a: By 2050, the figure will have risen to 40%.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: The population is projected to reach ten billion by 2050.

units.title: Choosing tenses for Task 1
units.summary: Match your tense to the dates on the chart, and stay consistent.

cards.title: Look at the time
cards.body:
- **Past dates** (1990–2010) → past simple; 'by 2010' → past perfect.
- **No dates / current data** → present simple.
- **Future dates / projections** → will, be expected to, be projected to, future perfect.
- **Past to future** (2000–2030) → past for the past part, future forms for the projection.
examples: Car ownership rose from 20% in 1990 to 45% in 2010.
The table shows that Japan has the highest life expectancy.
Car ownership is expected to reach 60% by 2030.

cards.title: Introduction verbs
cards.body: In the introduction, describe what the chart does in the **present simple**: *The bar chart compares…*, *The line graph illustrates…*, *The table gives information about…*
examples: The line graph illustrates changes in the consumption of three types of fast food between 1970 and 1990.

items: In 1995 the number increases to 300.
In 1995 the number increased to 300.
Past date → past tense.
The graph showed the population of four cities.
The graph shows the population of four cities.
The chart exists now → present simple.

cards.title: Use it in IELTS
cards.body: Mixing tenses for the same time period is one of the most common Task 1 errors and lowers Grammatical Range and Accuracy.
examples: While the number of cinema visits fell between 2000 and 2010, it is predicted to recover slightly by 2025.

practice.q: The pie chart ___ how household waste was disposed of in 2020.
Between 1980 and 2000, rice production ___ (double).
By 2000, the figure ___ (reach) its highest point.
The number of visitors ___ (expect) to rise to 5 million by 2030.
In 2005, unemployment [reaches] a peak of 9%.
practice.x: A past date needs the past simple.

practice.q: Choose the best sentence for a chart covering 2010–2030.
o: Solar power accounted for 5% in 2010 and is forecast to rise to 30% by 2030.
Solar power accounts for 5% in 2010 and rose to 30% by 2030.
Solar power accounted for 5% in 2010 and rises to 30% by 2030.
practice.a: Solar power accounted for 5% in 2010 and is forecast to rise to 30% by 2030.
practice.x: Past for 2010, future form for the projection.

practice.q: Put the words in order.
practice.a: The line graph illustrates changes in energy use between 1990 and 2020.
